subject: ventures/wash-and-fold-price-calculator
professional: a laundromat owner running wash-dry-fold and a pickup-and-delivery route, or a laundry-industry consultant who builds WDF cost models; first checks: is cost per pound built from loaded labour minutes, stepwise machine cycles at real capacity, supplies, delivery stops and overhead; is the margin (not markup) math right; does the minimum charge cover the smallest order; is fixed overhead treated as fixed when volume changes; can a delivery fee be modelled; are vehicle and utility defaults realistic

evidence.correctness: Ran computeWashAndFold on the page's own example (node /tmp/claude-0/wf.mjs) and recomputed by hand: loaded wage 16 x 1.18 = 18.88/h = 0.31467/min; labour (0.9 x 22 + 9) = 28.8 min = $9.06; machines ceil(22/20)=2 x 1.35 + ceil(22/30)=1 x 1.10 = $3.80; supplies $1.32; delivery 2 x (7 x 0.31467 + 4 x 0.55) = $8.81; overhead 2400/6000 x 22 = $8.80; total $31.79, $1.445/lb; all match the tool and the guide table. 10 lb order $21.52 matches (minimum-below-cost finding fires, loses $1.52). Target price 1.445/(1-0.35) = $2.2231 matches the textbook margin formula (not markup). But the profit-goal output is wrong: poundsForGoal = goal / profitPerPound (calculator.mjs:159-162) where profitPerPound already has fixed monthly overhead (rent, insurance, base utilities, software, index.html:172) spread at the current volume. Standard cost-volume-profit (required volume = (fixed + target profit) / contribution per unit): contribution 0.305 + 0.400 = $0.705/lb, so (2400 + 3000)/0.705 = 7,660 lb (349 orders), not 9,837 lb (448). The tool's own model run at monthlyPounds 9,837 reports $4,533.87 of profit, not $3,000; at 7,660 lb it reports $3,001.19. The headline volume is overstated by 28%. Core per-order arithmetic right, a displayed output wrong, so 2.
evidence.completeness: Every README feature works end to end: cost per order and per pound by component, break-even, target-margin price, margin at current price, monthly volume for a goal (works, but wrong; see correctness), findings below-break-even, minimum-below-cost, delivery-dominates, below-target-margin, no-overhead-allocated, partial-machine-load all exist and are tested; save/forget, share link, usage opt-out with DNT/GPC present (index.html:268-458, share.mjs, usage.mjs). Three content pages present and linked. No stubs or TODOs. served-copy.mjs reports no placeholder origin in llms.txt/sitemap.
evidence.verification: node --test *.test.mjs: 69 pass, 0 fail, 0.15 s. Five seeded mutants via quality_mutate.py: stepwise washer ceil removed caught; margin formula swapped to markup caught; delivery stops multiplier dropped caught; overhead halved caught; partial-load threshold >= -> > SURVIVED. 4 of 5 caught. The goal-volume test (calculator.test.mjs:91) pins goal/profitPerPound, i.e. it encodes the author's wrong belief, and no test checks the guide page's numbers against calculator output.
evidence.craft: Read calculator.mjs (281 lines), index.html script (268-458), share.mjs, tests. Single engine reused for the smallest order (costOfOrder exported), INPUT_FIELDS shared with share.mjs, money() sign handling. Defects: silent fallbacks, a blank or 0 washer/dryer capacity becomes 20 lb (calculator.mjs:112,114) with no message; targetMarginPct silently capped at 95 (line 132); money() duplicated in index.html:284 and calculator.mjs:274. Acceptable for a static tool.
evidence.claims: Checked 7 claims. Backed: guide cost table $31.79/$1.445, 10 lb $21.52 loss $1.52, $2.22 target, delivery $8.81 / counter $22.98 (recomputed); disclaimer and no-warranty on index, guide and both vs pages; privacy (grep finds no fetch/sendBeacon/XMLHttpRequest in any file); vs-cents states no Cents price or tier and disclaims affiliation. Not backed: guide 'Volume needed for target 9,837 lb (448 orders)', '175 more orders a month (~40/week)' (how-much-to-charge-for-wash-and-fold.html:90 and FAQ JSON-LD line 12) are wrong by the CVP check (349 orders, ~76 more); 'a dollar to two-fifty a pound, more in cities' (line 32) cites no file or source.
evidence.fitness: Walked the owner's job: enter own labour minutes, wage and payroll load, washer/dryer capacity and cycle cost, supplies, stops, overhead; get cost per pound, break-even, margin, and the minimum-charge check for the smallest accepted order. That job finishes and is the main value. Gaps: no delivery-fee or service-fee revenue input, although the tool's own finding recommends one (calculator.mjs:205), so an operator with a $4.99 delivery fee cannot see its effect; card processing is listed as fixed overhead though it is a % of revenue; the growth-planning output overstates volume needed.
evidence.domain: Stepwise machine cost, per-order fixed minutes, loaded wage and margin-not-markup are what a laundry consultant would build, done correctly. Departures: fixed overhead treated as a per-pound variable cost when solving for volume (CVP basic error); card fees modelled as fixed; example vehicle cost $0.55/mile vs IRS 2026 business standard mileage rate 72.5-76 cents (irs.gov, fetched 2026-11-19), the usual proxy for full vehicle cost, so the worked delivery cost is understated about $1.6-1.7 per order (input, but it is the published example); dryer and washer cost per cycle are inputs with no guidance beyond 'read your bills'.

defects.what: Volume for a monthly profit goal divides the goal by profit per pound that already includes fixed monthly overhead spread at today's volume, so overhead is treated as variable. Example: tool says 9,837 lb (448 orders) for $3,000; cost-volume-profit gives (2400+3000)/0.705 = 7,660 lb (349 orders), and the tool itself reports $4,533.87 profit at 9,837 lb. Overstates required volume by 28%
Guide page and its FAQ JSON-LD publish the wrong goal volume: '9,837 lb (448 orders)', '175 more a month (~40/week)'; correct about 7,660 lb, 349 orders, ~76 more

The goal-volume test pins goal/profitPerPound (the same wrong formula) instead of checking that the tool's own profit at the returned volume equals the goal; no test ties the guide's figures to calculator output
No delivery-fee or service-fee revenue input, although the delivery-dominates finding recommends a delivery fee; card processing is described as fixed overhead though it scales with revenue
Published example vehicle cost $0.55/mile is well under the IRS 2026 business standard rate (72.5-76 c), the common full-cost proxy, understating the worked delivery cost by about $1.7 per order
Market price range 'a dollar to two-fifty a pound, more in cities' has no cited source
Blank or zero washer/dryer capacity silently becomes 20 lb; partial-load threshold boundary (>=) untested (mutant survived)

verdict: A tidy, well-tested browser calculator whose core per-order costing is right: the 22 lb example ($31.79, $1.445/lb), the 10 lb minimum-charge loss ($1.52) and the 35% margin price ($2.2231, margin not markup) all recompute by hand, and 4 of 5 seeded bugs are caught. But its growth-planning output treats fixed monthly overhead as a per-pound cost when solving for volume: it tells the operator a $3,000 goal needs 9,837 lb (448 orders), while cost-volume-profit gives 7,660 lb (349 orders) and the tool itself reports $4,534 of profit at its own answer. The guide page publishes that wrong figure, and the unit test pins the wrong formula. No delivery-fee input exists despite the tool recommending one. Correctness and claims are 2, so it does not meet the bar; it is finished (completeness 3).
